chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:

“Whoever claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, is from something or in something or on something, then he has certainly disbelieved.” I said: “Explain that to me.” He (AS) responded, “I refer to a person who claims that He is contained by something, that He is restrained by something, or that He is preceded by something.”
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for God to be 'from', 'in', or 'on' something in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to articulate the principle of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence), arguing that attributing spatial dimensions or physical containment to Allah reduces the Creator to the level of created matter (*makhluq*). By negating that God is 'from', 'in', or 'on' anything, the Imam clarifies that divine essence is free from the limitations of place and direction, a core tenet in Shia theological discourse against anthropomorphism.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 5. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: al-Husayn ibn al-Husayn ibn Aban said, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sa`id, on the authority of al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, on the authority of `Asim ibn Humayd, on the authority of Abu Basir that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

“Whoever claims that Allah, the Mighty and High, is from something or in something or on something, then he has certainly disbelieved.” I said: “Explain that to me.” He (AS) responded, “I refer to a person who claims that He is contained by something, that He is restrained by something, or that He is preceded by something.”
